subject: Operational runbook & DPA execution plan for Acme Health
messages:
From: Samira Khan <skhan@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Acme DPA 2d redlines and execution preference

Laura,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our annotated DPA (Acme_DPA_annotated_v1.pdf). Two non-negotiable items from Acme privacy: 1) an initial incident notification to Acme within 24 hours of becoming aware of an incident that materially affects personal data; 2) 10 calendar days advance notice for any new subprocessor with a customer objection right.

We operate under healthcare regulator commitments so we need tight timelines. Please confirm whether Redwood can:

- Provide an initial notice within 24 hours of awareness, and follow-up updates at 72 hours and a final report within 14 days.
- Commit to 12 months of filtered audit log retention for our account and a mechanism to export logs for incident investigations.
- Reference the current EU transfer mechanism (SCCs or successor) and agree to reasonable cooperation with supervisory authorities.

We prefer AdobeSign for signature. Our procurement wants an exec-ready PDF by next Wednesday so we can route it for signature.

Regards,
Samira Khan
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

--
Attachment: Acme_DPA_annotated_v1.pdf (5 pages)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA 2d redlines and execution preference

Hi Samira,

Appreciate the annotated DPA. High level response below and a proposal for operational language that we think balances speed and accuracy: 

1) Notification timing: Redwood standard practice is initial notification within 48 hours of confirmation of unauthorized access. To accommodate Acme we propose hybrid language: initial notification within 24 hours of Redwood becoming aware AND confirming unauthorized access to Acme personal data; if confirmation requires third-party forensic work, Redwood will issue a preliminary notification within 48 hours that clearly states the investigation status and provide an update at 72 hours.

2) Forensics / reports: preliminary forensic highlights within 72 hours when available; a comprehensive report within 14 calendar days, subject to third-party vendor timelines. If additional time is required, Redwood will notify Acme and provide expected delivery dates.

3) Subprocessors: 10 calendar days notice is acceptable. We propose an objection/escalation ladder (written objection, technical call within 5 business days, executive escalation) rather than an immediate termination right.

4) Log retention: Redwood can commit to encrypted, filtered audit exports for 12 months and will provide account-level log exports for incident investigations under an NDA or lawful request.

5) Transfers: we will reference SCCs or successor transfer instruments and commit to cooperate with supervisory authorities.

We can produce an executive-ready DPA and push via AdobeSign if thats preferred. Attaching our tracked draft and an operational annex (Operational_Runbook_Acme_AnnexA.docx) with suggested timelines. Please confirm acceptance of the hybrid notification approach and well finalize for signature.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_hybrid_notice_track.pdf (4 pages); Attachment: Operational_Runbook_Acme_AnnexA.docx (3 pages)

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal - tech clarifications for Acme DPA runbook

Laura / Rishi,

A few technical points to support the annex: 
- \"Aware of an incident\" vs \"confirmed\" distinction: in our systems, "confirmation" requires validation (auth logs, data exfil traces, or vendor forensic confirmation). For edge cases we may take 242d72 hours to confirm.
- Preliminary packet: we can provide impacted data categories, estimated record counts, likely vector, and containment measures within 72 hours for most incidents. Full chain-of-custody reports are vendor-dependent.
- Logs: we can provide filtered, account-scoped audit exports for 12 months; we will not export raw system logs absent a lawful request.
- Subprocessor profile: security profile and relevant certifications can be produced within 3 business days of a notice.

I'll draft a short technical addendum paragraph for the annex and send it to you both.

Thanks,
Dev

(Internal)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal - tech clarifications for Acme DPA runbook

Agree with Dev. Two additional items for the runbook: 
- Escalation SLAs: technical call within 3 business days (instead of 5) given Acmes regulated environment, followed by a legal/ops alignment call within 5 business days if unresolved.
- Temporary mitigation options: support for dedicated routing to non-EU region or limited-scope token rotation if requested and feasible.

I'll include these in the addendum.

Best,
Rishi

(Internal)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Final operational language & AdobeSign envelope prep

Samira,

Thanks for reviewing the annex. Based on internal feedback we updated the operational annex and added the following final clauses to the DPA: 
- Incident notification: \"Redwood will provide Acme with an initial notification within 24 hours of Redwood's confirmation of unauthorized access to Acme personal data. If confirmation requires third-party forensic work, Redwood will provide a preliminary notification within 48 hours describing the investigation status and any known impact, and will provide an update at 72 hours.\"
- Forensic deliverables: preliminary forensic highlights within 72 hours where available; comprehensive report within 14 calendar days, subject to third-party vendor timelines; Redwood will notify Acme if additional time is required.
- Subprocessor change: 10 calendar days notice; Acme may object in writing; Redwood will schedule a technical call within 3 business days and pursue mitigation options within 10 business days before termination remedies are considered.
- Logs: Redwood will retain encrypted, filtered audit logs for 12 months and provide account-scoped exports for incident investigations under NDA or lawful request.
- Transfers: DPA will reference SCCs or successor instruments and Redwood will cooperate with supervisory authorities.

We prepared an exec-ready PDF and created an AdobeSign envelope per your preference. Envelope link attached. Please confirm and we will route for signature tonight.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
